<header class="dg-head dg-head-section"><p class="dg-kicker">Chapter 6 <span class="dg-sep">•</span> <a href="index.html">Covariant Derivative</a></p><h1 class="dg-title"><span class="dg-secnum">6.1</span> Connections and Affine Manifolds</h1></header>
<ul class="dg-itemize dg-depth-1">
<li><p>A (linear) <strong>connection</strong> <span class="math inline">\(\nabla\)</span> on a smooth manifold <span class="math inline">\((\mathcal{M}, \mathcal{O}, \mathcal{A})\)</span> assigns to every tangent vector <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{X}_p \in T_p\mathcal{M}\)</span>, at any point <span class="math inline">\(p \in \mathcal{M}\)</span>, and to every tensor field <span class="math inline">\(T \in \Gamma T^{(r,s)}\mathcal{M}\)</span>, of any valence <span class="math inline">\((r,s)\)</span>, a tensor at <span class="math inline">\(p\)</span>,  <span class="math display">\begin{align*}
            \nabla : T_p\mathcal{M} \times \Gamma T^{(r,s)}\mathcal{M} &amp;\longrightarrow T_p^{(r,s)}\mathcal{M} \\
            (\mathcal{X}_p, T) &amp;\longmapsto \nabla(\mathcal{X}_p, T) \coloneqq \nabla_{\mathcal{X}_p} T,
        \end{align*}</span>  called the <strong>covariant derivative</strong> of <span class="math inline">\(T\)</span> along <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{X}_p\)</span><sup class="dg-fnref"><a href="#fn-1" id="fnref-1" role="doc-noteref" aria-label="Footnote 1">1</a></sup>, satisfying, for all <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{X}_p, \mathcal{Y}_p \in T_p\mathcal{M}\)</span>, <span class="math inline">\(\alpha \in \mathbb{R}\)</span>, <span class="math inline">\(f \in C^\infty(\mathcal{M})\)</span> and <span class="math inline">\(T_1, T_2 \in \Gamma T^{(r,s)}\mathcal{M}\)</span>:</p>
<ol class="dg-enumerate dg-depth-1">
<li><p><em>Action on scalar fields:</em>  <span class="math inline">\(\nabla_{\mathcal{X}_p} f = \mathcal{X}_p(f)\)</span>.</p></li>
<li><p><em>Additivity in the tensor field:</em>  <span class="math inline">\(\nabla_{\mathcal{X}_p} (T_1 \oplus_\Gamma T_2) = \nabla_{\mathcal{X}_p} T_1 \oplus_\Gamma \nabla_{\mathcal{X}_p} T_2\)</span>.</p></li>
<li><p><em>Leibniz rule:</em> using as an example a <span class="math inline">\((1,1)\)</span>-tensor field <span class="math inline">\(T\)</span>, for all <span class="math inline">\(\mathsf{X} \in \Gamma T^*\mathcal{M}\)</span> and <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{Y} \in \Gamma T\mathcal{M}\)</span>,  <span class="math display">\[
                    \nabla_{\mathcal{X}_p} \big( T(\mathsf{X}, \mathcal{Y}) \big)
                    = (\nabla_{\mathcal{X}_p} T)(\mathsf{X}_p, \mathcal{Y}_p)
                    \oplus_\Gamma T_p(\nabla_{\mathcal{X}_p} \mathsf{X}, \mathcal{Y}_p)
                    \oplus_\Gamma T_p(\mathsf{X}_p, \nabla_{\mathcal{X}_p} \mathcal{Y}),
                \]</span>  where the left-hand side is the covariant derivative of the scalar field <span class="math inline">\(T(\mathsf{X}, \mathcal{Y})\)</span>, and analogously for tensor fields of any valence, with one term per argument.</p></li>
<li><p><em>linearity in the direction:</em>  <span class="math inline">\(\nabla_{\alpha \mathcal{X}_p + \mathcal{Y}_p} T = \alpha \, \nabla_{\mathcal{X}_p} T \oplus_\Gamma \nabla_{\mathcal{Y}_p} T\)</span>.</p></li>
<li><p><em>Smoothness:</em> for every vector field <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{X} \in \Gamma T\mathcal{M}\)</span>, the map <span class="math inline">\(p \mapsto \nabla_{\mathcal{X}(p)} T\)</span> is a smooth tensor field, denoted <span class="math inline">\(\nabla_\mathcal{X} T \in \Gamma T^{(r,s)}\mathcal{M}\)</span>.</p></li>
</ol>
<p>The two arguments play different roles. The direction enters only through a single tangent vector at <span class="math inline">\(p\)</span>, whereas the tensor field is genuinely differentiated: <span class="math inline">\(\nabla_{\mathcal{X}_p} T\)</span> depends on the values of <span class="math inline">\(T\)</span> around <span class="math inline">\(p\)</span>. Letting the direction vary with a vector field, property 5 yields the field-level map  <span class="math display">\begin{align*}
            \nabla : \Gamma T\mathcal{M} \times \Gamma T^{(r,s)}\mathcal{M} &amp;\longrightarrow \Gamma T^{(r,s)}\mathcal{M} \\
            (\mathcal{X}, T) &amp;\longmapsto \nabla_\mathcal{X} T,
        \end{align*}</span>  which, applying property 4 at each point with <span class="math inline">\(\alpha = f(p)\)</span>, is <span class="math inline">\(C^\infty(\mathcal{M})\)</span>-linear in the vector field,  <span class="math display">\[
            \nabla_{f \odot_\Gamma \mathcal{X} \oplus_\Gamma \mathcal{Y}} T = f \odot_\Gamma \nabla_{\mathcal{X}} T \oplus_\Gamma \nabla_{\mathcal{Y}} T
            \qquad \forall \, f \in C^\infty(\mathcal{M}), \; \mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y} \in \Gamma T\mathcal{M}.
        \]</span>  Many texts take this field-level map as the definition, with <span class="math inline">\(C^\infty(\mathcal{M})\)</span>-linearity as an axiom. Both definitions are equivalent<sup class="dg-fnref"><a href="#fn-2" id="fnref-2" role="doc-noteref" aria-label="Footnote 2">2</a></sup>, but the pointwise one is the natural one for differentiating along curves, where the direction is the velocity of the curve, only available at the points of the curve. From now onwards, sums of fields and their s-multiplication by scalar fields are written as <span class="math inline">\(+\)</span> and juxtaposition (instead of <span class="math inline">\(\oplus_\Gamma\)</span>, <span class="math inline">\(\odot_\Gamma\)</span> and their starred counterparts)</p></li>
<li><p>An <strong>affine manifold</strong> is the quadruple <span class="math inline">\((\mathcal{M}, \mathcal{O}, \mathcal{A}, \nabla)\)</span>, i.e. a smooth manifold equipped with a connection.</p></li>
<li><p><em>Product rule.</em> Properties 1 and 3 imply, for all <span class="math inline">\(g \in C^\infty(\mathcal{M})\)</span> and <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{Y} \in \Gamma T\mathcal{M}\)</span>,  <span class="math display">\[
            \nabla_{\mathcal{X}_p} (g \, \mathcal{Y}) = \mathcal{X}_p(g) \, \mathcal{Y}_p + g(p) \, \nabla_{\mathcal{X}_p} \mathcal{Y},
        \]</span>  and likewise <span class="math inline">\(\nabla_{\mathcal{X}_p}(g \, T) = \mathcal{X}_p(g) \, T_p + g(p) \, \nabla_{\mathcal{X}_p} T\)</span> for tensor fields of any valence. Indeed, regarding <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{Y}\)</span> as a <span class="math inline">\((1,0)\)</span>-tensor field, <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{Y}(\mathsf{X}) \coloneqq \mathsf{X}\left\lceil \mathcal{Y} \right\rfloor\)</span>, the Leibniz rule reads <span class="math inline">\(\nabla_{\mathcal{X}_p} \big( \mathcal{Y}(\mathsf{X}) \big) = (\nabla_{\mathcal{X}_p} \mathcal{Y})(\mathsf{X}_p) + \mathcal{Y}_p(\nabla_{\mathcal{X}_p} \mathsf{X})\)</span>. Applying it to <span class="math inline">\(g\,\mathcal{Y}\)</span>, and evaluating the left-hand side with property 1 and the product rule of tangent vectors acting on products of scalar fields<sup class="dg-fnref"><a href="#fn-3" id="fnref-3" role="doc-noteref" aria-label="Footnote 3">3</a></sup>,  <span class="math display">\begin{align*}
            \big( \nabla_{\mathcal{X}_p}(g\,\mathcal{Y}) \big)(\mathsf{X}_p) + g(p) \, \mathcal{Y}_p(\nabla_{\mathcal{X}_p} \mathsf{X})
            &amp;= \nabla_{\mathcal{X}_p} \big( g \, \mathcal{Y}(\mathsf{X}) \big)
            = \mathcal{X}_p(g) \, \mathcal{Y}_p(\mathsf{X}_p) + g(p) \, \mathcal{X}_p\big( \mathcal{Y}(\mathsf{X}) \big) \\
            &amp;= \mathcal{X}_p(g) \, \mathcal{Y}_p(\mathsf{X}_p) + g(p) \, (\nabla_{\mathcal{X}_p} \mathcal{Y})(\mathsf{X}_p)
            + g(p) \, \mathcal{Y}_p(\nabla_{\mathcal{X}_p} \mathsf{X}).
        \end{align*}</span>  The terms <span class="math inline">\(g(p) \, \mathcal{Y}_p(\nabla_{\mathcal{X}_p} \mathsf{X})\)</span> cancel and, since every covector at <span class="math inline">\(p\)</span> is the value of some covector field (Section <a class="dg-xref" href="../tangent-spaces/cotangent-space.html" data-kind="section" data-label="section_Cotangent_Space">4.2</a>), the product rule follows.</p></li>
</ul>
<section class="dg-footnotes" role="doc-endnotes"><div class="dg-fn" id="fn-1" role="doc-footnote"><a class="dg-fn-num" href="#fnref-1" aria-label="Back to the text">1</a><div class="dg-fn-body"><p>In this text, the terms covariant derivative and connection are used interchangeably. In these notes the connection is the whole structure <span class="math inline">\(\nabla\)</span>, while the covariant derivative is what it produces, <span class="math inline">\(\nabla_{\mathcal{X}_p} T\)</span>. In a more general setting, however, a connection is a strictly more general notion than a covariant derivative; see Appendix <a class="dg-xref" href="../proofs-and-additional-material/connection-vs-covariant-derivative.html" data-kind="section" data-label="section_Connection_vs_Covariant_Derivative">B.9</a>.</p></div></div><div class="dg-fn" id="fn-2" role="doc-footnote"><a class="dg-fn-num" href="#fnref-2" aria-label="Back to the text">2</a><div class="dg-fn-body"><p><span class="math inline">\(C^\infty(\mathcal{M})\)</span>-linearity implies that <span class="math inline">\((\nabla_\mathcal{X} T)(p)\)</span> depends on <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{X}\)</span> only through <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{X}(p)\)</span>: in a chart, <span class="math inline">\(\left. \mathcal{X} \right|_\mathcal{U} = x^i \, \partial x_i\)</span> gives <span class="math inline">\((\nabla_\mathcal{X} T)(p) = x^i(p) \, (\nabla_{\partial x_i} T)(p)\)</span>. Hence <span class="math inline">\(\nabla_{\mathcal{X}_p} T \coloneqq (\nabla_\mathcal{X} T)(p)\)</span>, for any <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{X}\)</span> with <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{X}(p) = \mathcal{X}_p\)</span>, is well defined.</p></div></div><div class="dg-fn" id="fn-3" role="doc-footnote"><a class="dg-fn-num" href="#fnref-3" aria-label="Back to the text">3</a><div class="dg-fn-body"><p><span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{X}_p(g h) = \mathcal{X}_p(g) \, h(p) + g(p) \, \mathcal{X}_p(h)\)</span>, which follows from the product rule of ordinary derivatives applied to <span class="math inline">\(\big( (g h) \circ \gamma \big)'(\lambda_0)\)</span>.</p></div></div></section>
